# Search as navigation: what changed in v1.1.0

From v1.0.0 (2026-10-18, `e9fbb78e9`) to v1.1.0 (2026-10-18, this release), paragraph by paragraph.

0 paragraphs added, 0 removed, 2 changed in place, 42 unchanged. About 3 words added and 0 removed. Insertions are marked like this, deletions like this; unchanged runs are folded to one line; figures appear as their file names.

[all versions](../search-as-navigation.md)

16 unchanged paragraphs, under In short {#in-short}, What search is today {#today}, Search as navigation {#navigation}

What I wanthave in mind is closer to walking than to asking. Say I type *Portugal*. I should see the articles about Portugal, but also the graph around them: the ideas they share, the people and companies they mention, the wire stories, the other articles they link to. I should see their sections as one-liners, so I can tell in a few seconds which part of which article is the one I want. I should see their figures as a collage, because many of these articles have good images, and an image is often how I remember a piece.

6 unchanged paragraphs, under Deterministic first {#deterministic}, The pane that shows the working {#pane}

I wantwould like a pane on the side that shows exactly what is happening. It is how I will debug this, and it is what a power user will want: every file fetched, its size and how long it took; how each word resolved, and by which rule; each step of the walk and how many nodes it touched; why each result is there, and its score; the same query as SQL and as SPARQL, editable; and the time each stage took, from loading to drawing.

20 unchanged paragraphs, under The taxonomy debt {#debt}, Why a clean graph should beat vectors {#vectors}, What the brief asks for {#brief}…
